slides.title: Dark before morning
slides.text: Lanterns on the tower stair keep going dark before morning. Nobody has checked how fast each one burns its oil. Tally taps a tank: 12 milliliters gone in 4 hours. How much is that for each hour?

slides.title: A rate for just 1
slides.text: A rate compares two different units, such as milliliters and hours. Share the 12 milliliters equally over the 4 hours: 12 ÷ 4 = 3. The unit rate is 3 milliliters per hour, the amount for exactly 1 hour.

visual.label: A double number line of oil burned over time: 3 milliliters in 1 hour, 6 in 2, 9 in 3 and 12 in 4

focus.cue: What the tank showed: 12 milliliters in 4 hours.
Shared equally, each hour burns 3: the unit rate.

slides.title: Use the unit rate
slides.text: Once you know the amount for 1 hour, any number of hours is one multiplication. At 3 milliliters per hour, 7 hours needs 7 × 3 = 21 milliliters. Adding 3 and 7 would answer a different question.

visual.label: A rate table at 3 milliliters per hour: 1 hour burns 3, 2 hours 6, 4 hours 12 and 7 hours 21
head: Hours

focus.cue: The unit rate: 1 hour burns 3 milliliters.
7 hours burn 7 times as much: 21 milliliters.

slides.title: From 4 hours to 10 hours
slides.text: Another lantern burns 6 milliliters in 4 hours, and its tank must last 10 hours. The rate is not given for 1 hour, so find that first. Then multiply by the hours you need.

visual.label: A double number line at 1.5 milliliters per hour: 3 milliliters in 2 hours, 6 in 4, 9 in 6, 12 in 8 and 15 in 10

focus.cue: The lantern burns 6 milliliters in 4 hours.
Half of that: 3 milliliters in 2 hours.
Five steps of 2 hours make 10 hours: 15 milliliters.

slides.title: Compare with unit rates
slides.text: Lantern A burns 9 milliliters in 3 hours. Lantern B burns 10 milliliters in 5 hours. Their unit rates are 3 and 2 milliliters per hour, so B burns less each hour and the same tank lasts longer.

visual.label: A bar chart of two unit rates: lantern A burns 3 milliliters per hour and lantern B burns 2

focus.cue: Lantern B: 10 ÷ 5 = 2 per hour. It burns less.

slides.title: Words to know
slides.text: Four words for working with rates.

words.means: a ratio that compares two different units, such as milliliters and hours
the amount for exactly 1 of the second unit, such as 3 milliliters per hour
for each one, as in 50 meters per minute
two number lines, one above the other, whose matching marks are equal ratios

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Lantern Mix at Burn Rate. Find what each lantern burns in 1 hour, then fill its tank so it lasts the night. Six lanterns finish the step.
slides.alt: Lantern Mix on a phone: a double number line of 12 milliliters in 4 hours on the board, and a dial to set.
